items.heading: Two Answers Dominate When People
items.text: Two Answers Dominate When People Two Answers Dominate When People Two answers dominate when people search this exact question: "follow your passion" and "chase the highest-paying field." Both feel like complete advice. Neither one is.

items.heading: Whether There Is Real Room
items.text: Whether there is real room to advance, specialise, lead, consult, or own - or whether the role caps out fast.

items.heading: Score Each of the 8
items.text: Score Each of the 8 Score each of the 8 factors 1 to 5 for how much it matters to you right now. Not universally, and not how it "should" matter. A parent supporting a family scores stability differently than a 19-year-old testing a first real option.

items.heading: List Your Shortlisted Options Side
items.text: List your shortlisted options side by side. Two or three real options, not an open-ended brainstorm.

items.heading: Score Each Option 1
items.text: Score each option 1 to 5 on each factor, using real evidence. Job postings, salary data, a conversation with someone doing the work, or a small test project - not a gut feeling.

items.heading: Multiply Your Importance Score
items.text: Multiply your importance score by each option's factor score, then add the totals. The highest total is not an automatic verdict, but it is a far better starting point than an unweighted gut call.

items.heading: Re
items.text: Re-run it after any real test. A short proof project or one honest conversation with someone in the field usually changes at least one score - treat the first pass as a draft, not a final answer.
